History of the West Midlands.fact: This area was based on the seven county boroughs and four other non-county boroughs and urban districts around the fringe of the conurbation – Aldridge-Brownhills, Halesowen, Stourbridge, and Sutton Coldfield. The area was divided into seven new metropolitan boroughs – Aldridge-Brownhills was added to Walsall; Halesowen and Stourbridge to Dudley and Sutton Coldfield to Birmingham.

History of the West Midlands.question: The _____ reform created a West Midlands County Council that covered the entire area and dealt with strategic issues
History of the West Midlands.fact: The 1974 reform created a West Midlands County Council that covered the entire area and dealt with strategic issues.

History of the West Midlands.question: Margaret Thatcher's government abolished the metropolitan county councils with the Local Government Act _____, in 1986, causing the seven metropolitan boroughs to become de facto unitary authorities
History of the West Midlands.fact: Margaret Thatcher's government abolished the metropolitan county councils with the Local Government Act 1985, in 1986, causing the seven metropolitan boroughs to become de facto unitary authorities.

History of the West Midlands.subject: Environment & Ecology
History of the West Midlands.question: This move also saw the abolition of the _____ as well as the metropolitan councils for Merseyside, Greater Manchester, Tyne and Wear, Humberside and Avon
History of the West Midlands.fact: This move also saw the abolition of the Greater London Council as well as the metropolitan councils for Merseyside, Greater Manchester, Tyne and Wear, Humberside and Avon.
